name: Bandwagon
shortDef: Treating something as true or good because many people believe or do it.
definition: Concluding that a claim is true, or a choice is right, because it's popular, trending or what most people do, when popularity isn't evidence about the question being asked.
howToSpot: Is the main reason how many people believe, buy or do it?
Ask what evidence those people had, and whether it applies to you
Watch for sales figures, trends or lines out the door standing in for reasons
classicExample: Three million people have downloaded this diet app, so it must actually work.
legitimateVersion: Popularity is fair evidence when the question is about popularity itself, like which time slot most families prefer, or when many users report on something they judge directly, like comfort.

contrast.fal_appeal_to_authority: Bandwagon leans on how many people agree; appeal to authority leans on one esteemed source.
contrast.fal_appeal_to_tradition: Bandwagon says lots of people do it now; appeal to tradition says it's always been done that way.
